cards.headline: The chanted commands got sampled by Busta Rhymes
cards.snippet: Daft Punk's "Technologic" (2005, from the album Human After All) features an electronically transposed voice chanting technological commands. Part of those altered vocals was sampled in the Busta Rhymes single "Touch It", produced by Swizz Beatz. Elements of "Touch It" and "Technologic" were later remixed together and included on Daft Punk's live album Alive 2007. The French duo's robotic voice thus went into hip-hop and returned to their own live show.
cards.context: The song's robotic voice became raw material for hip-hop and then came back into Daft Punk's live show.

cards.headline: The video puts a tiny robot in a pyramid inside a bigger pyramid
cards.snippet: In the music video for Daft Punk's "Technologic" (2005), a small robot character appears to chant the lyrics inside a pyramid-themed stage. Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo said the duo thought it would be funny to put the two of them in a bigger pyramid. The robot was created by Tony Gardner and his team at Alterian, Inc. The pyramid design is similar to the staging Daft Punk used on their Alive 2006/2007 tour.
cards.context: The pyramid look echoes the staging of the Alive 2006/2007 tour.

cards.headline: Alive 2007: Technologic blended into Touch It, Robot Rock and Voyager
cards.snippet: Recorded live at Daft Punk's Alive 2007 show, this set folds "Technologic" into a continuous mix with Touch It, Oh Yeah and Voyager instead of playing it straight.
cards.context: The mashup links Daft Punk's live show to the Busta Rhymes track that sampled the song.
